title: Scylla Manager
description: Scylla Manager health check, repair and backup, built on the per task metrics from CLOUD-327.

panels.title: SM node memory used
panels.description: Memory in use on the node running Scylla Manager, against MemAvailable rather than MemFree - free memory excludes the page cache, which the kernel will hand back under pressure, so it reads alarmingly low on a perfectly healthy host.

panels.title: SM node swap used
panels.description: Swap in use on the Scylla Manager node. The denominator is clamped so a host with no swap configured reads 0 rather than dividing by zero and rendering NaN. Worth watching at lower numbers than the other two: a host that has started swapping at all is already short of memory.

panels.title: SM node CPU busy
panels.description: CPU in use on the Scylla Manager node, averaged across cores over 5 minutes - so it is a share of the whole host, not of one core, and cannot exceed 100. Derived from idle time, which is the only mode guaranteed to be present on every platform.

panels.title: Scylla Manager -> cluster nodes connectivity health check
CQL
panels.description: Left: nodes not healthy right now. Right: nodes that were not healthy for the whole selected range, so a node that dropped and recovered is still counted.

panels.title: REST
panels.description: Left: nodes not healthy right now. Right: nodes that were not healthy for the whole selected range, so a node that dropped and recovered is still counted.

panels.title: Alternator
panels.description: Left: nodes not healthy right now. Right: nodes that were not healthy for the whole selected range, so a node that dropped and recovered is still counted. Scylla Manager reports a node as up with 0ms latency when the Alternator API is not enabled, so ALL UP here means "not broken", not "in use".

panels.title: Nodes not healthy for the whole range
panels.description: Empty when every node was up for the entire selected range. A node that dropped and recovered before now is still listed, with the protocol whose check failed - or a single "Agent" row when the node could not be reached at all, in which case the protocols say nothing and are not listed.

targets.expr: label_replace(min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_cql_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -1, "protocol", "CQL", "", "") or label_replace(min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_rest_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -1, "protocol", "REST", "", "") or label_replace(min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_alternator_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -1, "protocol", "Alternator", "", "") or label_replace(min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_rest_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -2, "protocol", "Agent", "", "")

panels.title: CQL status
panels.description:
Three values exist, ordered by severity: up, this protocol's own check failing, and the agent not answering at all. The last one drops the line lowest, because Scylla Manager cannot see the node and the protocol's state is unknown rather than bad.

Only those three positions are meaningful - there is no value in between - so the axis is drawn without decimals and every tick names a state.

In the legend, Last is the state now and Min is the worst state the node reached in the range: the encoding is ordered, so the minimum is literally the worst. Last OK with a lower Min means the node dropped and recovered, which on a wide range can be a few pixels wide on the line.

panels.title: Repair tasks
panels.description: Every repair task: how its last known run went, then how the task is configured. State, progress and the age of the last success describe the last run - progress is not gated on the task running, so for a run that failed or was stopped it shows how far it got. An empty progress cell means there is none to report. A property the user did not configure is shown with the value the task will actually run with: the Scylla Manager default, "all" where an empty filter means every datacenter or host, and "incremental" where SM sends no mode and Scylla applies its own default. Scheduled tasks are always listed; ad-hoc ones only when the selected time range covers their run.

targets.expr: max by (task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="repair"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}))

(max by (task) ((time() - scylla_manager_scheduler_task_last_success_seconds{cluster="$cluster", type="repair"}) and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}))) or (max by (task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}) * 0 + 99999999)
max by (task) (scylla_manager_repair_task_progress{cluster="$cluster"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}))

panels.title: Repair task state
panels.description:
One row per repair task, labelled by task name - unnamed tasks fall back to their task ID. type=repair covers vnode and tablet repair tasks.

The bands carry colour only and the legend is the key. Nothing is written on the row because the state is latched: on a wide range a band covers most of the row, and text across all of it drowns the runs that actually matter.

Hover a band to read it: a run in flight reports its percentage, a finished one its state. The colour key is the strip below rather than the panel's own legend - that legend is built from the distinct values in the data, so leaving the percentages unmapped for the tooltip would make it list every percentage ever seen as its own entry.

targets.expr: (max by (task) (scylla_manager_repair_task_progress{cluster="$cluster"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="repair"} == 1)) or max by (task) ((scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="repair"} != 1) - 10)) * on(task) group_left(name) (topk(1, scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}) by (task))

options.content: 🔵 **RUNNING**  🟢 **PREV EXECUTION SUCCEEDED**  🔴 **PREV EXECUTION FAILED**  🟡 **PREV EXECUTION STOPPED**  ⚪ **NEVER EXECUTED YET**

panels.title: Backup tasks
panels.description: Every backup task: how its last known run went, then how the task is configured. Retention and Retention days are not independent - SM keeps 3 backups only when neither is set, and otherwise honours the one that is and treats the other as 0. Scheduled tasks are always listed; ad-hoc ones only when the selected time range covers their run.

targets.expr: max by (task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="backup"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}))

(max by (task) ((time() - scylla_manager_scheduler_task_last_success_seconds{cluster="$cluster", type="backup"}) and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}))) or (max by (task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}) * 0 + 99999999)
max by (task) (scylla_manager_backup_task_progress{cluster="$cluster"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}))

panels.title: Backup task state
panels.description:
One row per backup task, labelled by task name - unnamed tasks fall back to their task ID.

The bands carry colour only, keyed by the strip below. Nothing is written on the row because the state is latched: on a wide range a band covers most of the row, and text across all of it drowns the runs that actually matter.

Hover a band to read it: a run in flight reports its percentage, and a finished one reports its state. The colour key is a strip rather than the panel's own legend - that legend is built from the distinct values in the data, so leaving the percentages unmapped for the tooltip would make it list every percentage ever seen as its own entry.

targets.expr: (max by (task) (scylla_manager_backup_task_progress{cluster="$cluster"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="backup"} == 1)) or max by (task) ((scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="backup"} != 1) - 10)) * on(task) group_left(name) (topk(1, scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}) by (task))
